questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: Question 2. Which combination best defines an epithelial lining?

options.text: Widely separated cells in abundant collagen bundles
options.explanation: Abundant collagen separating relatively sparse cells favours connective tissue rather than an epithelial lining.

options.text: Closely joined cells with apical–basal polarity and little intervening matrix
options.explanation: A continuous cellular boundary, polarity and minimal intervening matrix together support epithelial tissue. The basal surface attaches to a basal lamina.

options.text: Elongated contractile cells arranged in deep bundles
options.explanation: This describes a muscle pattern. A luminal epithelial boundary is identified by its cell relationships and surface organisation.

questions.title: Histology Foundations: The Four Basic Tissues
questions.subject: histology
questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: Question 3. What is the principal mechanical role of parallel collagen bundles in a tendon?

options.text: Generate active force by actin–myosin sliding
options.explanation: Muscle cells generate active force through actin and myosin. Tendon collagen transmits tensile force; it does not contract through sarcomeres.

options.text: Conduct action potentials between the muscle and bone
options.explanation: Axons conduct action potentials. The main role of tendon collagen is mechanical force transmission, not electrical communication.

options.text: Resist and transmit tensile loading mainly along the bundle axis
options.explanation: Parallel collagen provides strength in the principal direction of pull. Fibroblasts maintain this extracellular matrix.

questions.title: Histology Foundations: The Four Basic Tissues
questions.subject: histology
questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: Question 4. Which pattern most strongly supports skeletal muscle in a longitudinal section?

options.text: Long striated fibres with multiple peripheral nuclei
options.explanation: The combination of sarcomeric striations, multinucleation and peripheral nuclear position supports skeletal muscle.

options.text: Branching striated cells with central nuclei and intercalated discs
options.explanation: This combination favours cardiac muscle; striations alone cannot distinguish skeletal from cardiac muscle.

options.text: Spindle-shaped cells with single central nuclei and no cross-striations
options.explanation: This is the expected smooth-muscle pattern. Smooth muscle still has actin and myosin, but lacks sarcomeres.

questions.title: Histology Foundations: The Four Basic Tissues
questions.subject: histology
questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: Question 5. Which pairing correctly identifies a myelin-forming glial cell and its location?

options.text: Oligodendrocyte — peripheral nerve
options.explanation: Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin. Peripheral myelin is formed by Schwann cells.

options.text: Schwann cell — peripheral nerve
options.explanation: A myelinating Schwann cell forms one internode of one PNS axon. Many successive cells are needed along a long myelinated axon.

options.text: Fibroblast — central nervous system axon
options.explanation: Fibroblasts produce connective-tissue matrix. They are not the glial cells that form CNS myelin.

questions.title: Histology Foundations: The Four Basic Tissues
questions.subject: histology
questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: Question 6. Which statement correctly links a tissue to a representative location and function?

options.text: Nervous tissue — tendon collagen transmitting tensile force
options.explanation: The collagen bundles of a tendon are connective tissue. Nervous tissue transmits and integrates signals through neurons with glial support.

options.text: Muscle tissue — the simple squamous lining of a blood vessel
options.explanation: The vessel lining is endothelial epithelium. Smooth muscle may be present deeper in the wall, where it regulates vessel calibre.

options.text: Connective tissue — loose supporting tissue beneath an epithelium
options.explanation: Loose connective tissue supports epithelial sheets and contains matrix, resident or recruited cells and often vessels that supply the nearby lining.

questions.title: Anatomy Foundations: Position, Planes and Organisation

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the wrist relative to the elbow along the upper limb?

options.text: Coronal

options.text: Parasagittal
options.explanation: A parasagittal plane is parallel to the median plane but displaced from it, separating unequal right and left portions.

questions.prompt: Which boundary separates the thoracic and abdominopelvic compartments?

options.text: The pelvic brim as a complete muscular partition
options.explanation: The pelvic brim marks a regional boundary; it is not a sealed partition. Abdominal and pelvic subdivisions communicate.

questions.prompt: What is the normal anatomical relationship of the pleural cavity to the lung?

options.text: It is the air-containing lumen of the lung
options.explanation: Air normally moves through respiratory passages and air spaces. Those are distinct from the space between pleural layers.

options.text: It is the potential space between visceral and parietal pleura
options.explanation: Visceral pleura covers the lung and parietal pleura lines the compartment. The intervening thin fluid-containing space is the pleural cavity.

options.text: It is the entire thoracic compartment including the mediastinum
options.explanation: The thorax includes more than the pleural spaces. The mediastinum lies centrally between the right and left pleural compartments.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: Which classification best describes the stomach?

options.text: One type of muscle tissue
options.explanation: Smooth muscle is one component of the wall. The organ also contains epithelial, connective and nervous tissue.

options.text: An organ system consisting only of glands
options.explanation: An organ system coordinates multiple organs. The stomach is one organ and includes more than its glands.

options.text: An organ integrating several tissue families

questions.title: Anatomy Foundations: Position, Planes and Organisation
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: Which pair of structures is ipsilateral?

options.text: The right hand and the right foot

options.text: The right hand and the left hand

options.text: The left knee and the right ankle
options.explanation: These are on opposite sides. Both belong to lower limbs, but that does not make them ipsilateral.

questions.title: Physiology Foundations: Membrane Transport and Resting Potential

questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: What does an intracellular recording of −70 mV mean when the extracellular electrode is the reference?

options.text: The inside is 70 mV more negative than the outside.
options.explanation: Membrane voltage is defined here as inside minus outside, so a negative value places the inside below the reference.

options.text: Every resting human cell must have exactly this voltage.
options.explanation: Resting voltages vary by cell type and conditions; −70 mV is an illustrative neuronal value.

options.text: The outside is 70 mV more negative than the inside.
options.explanation: The stated recording is inside minus outside; a negative reading means the inside is more negative.

questions.title: Biochemistry Foundations: Enzymes, Kinetics and Regulation
questions.subject: biochemistry
questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: An enzyme is added to a reversible reaction without changing temperature or starting composition. What does catalysis change?

options.text: The equilibrium constant, favouring more product.
options.explanation: Catalysis changes the route and speed of reaction, not the thermodynamic equilibrium constant.

options.text: The rate at which equilibrium is approached.
options.explanation: Lowering activation barriers speeds forward and reverse reactions, so equilibrium is reached sooner without being shifted.

options.text: The overall free-energy difference between reactants and products.
options.explanation: The free-energy difference is a thermodynamic property of the states, not of the catalytic pathway.

questions.title: Genetics Foundations: Genome, Inheritance and Gene Expression
questions.subject: genetics
questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: Which process makes RNA using a DNA template?

options.text: Replication
options.explanation: Replication copies DNA into DNA; it is distinct from production of an RNA transcript.

options.text: Translation
options.explanation: Translation uses an mRNA sequence to build a polypeptide at a ribosome.

options.text: Transcription
options.explanation: Transcription makes an RNA molecule using one DNA strand as the template.

questions.title: Biophysics Foundations: Diffusion, Osmosis and Membranes
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.heading: Knowledge Check
questions.prompt: For a neutral solute with rate = D × A × Δc / L, only barrier thickness L doubles. What happens to the steady transfer rate?

options.text: It halves.
options.explanation: Thickness is in the denominator; doubling it halves the rate with D, area and concentration difference fixed.

options.text: It doubles.
options.explanation: That would follow from doubling area or concentration difference, not thickness.

options.text: It stays the same.
options.explanation: The diffusion path is longer, so unchanged area alone cannot preserve the rate under this model.

questions.title: Observation versus whole-follicle inference
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: In a fictional follicular profile, no cavity is visible in the available section. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: No cavity is demonstrated in this section
options.explanation: This states the actual observation. A feature outside the section plane can remain unseen.

options.text: No cavity exists anywhere in the whole follicle
options.explanation: That stronger claim needs evidence beyond the single profile. The section-plane model gives a counterexample.

options.text: The person’s exact cycle day has been identified
options.explanation: The observation does not provide an exact cycle date or clinical outcome.

questions.title: Sequence change versus selection
questions.subject: genetics
questions.prompt: A fictional worksheet changes a rearranged variable label from V0 to V1. It supplies no binding assay or observations of which cell variants contributed afterward. What is established within the model?

options.text: A stipulated sequence difference, with binding improvement and selection still unmeasured.
options.explanation: The changed label records the specified difference. It does not supply an affinity comparison or evidence about later contribution to the response.

options.text: Improved binding and successful selection, because every new variable sequence is better.
options.explanation: A mutation creates a different candidate; its functional result and contribution require separate evidence. The worksheet does not establish either.

options.text: A heavy-chain class switch, because any V-label change replaces the constant region.
options.explanation: The V label concerns the rearranged variable sequence. A class-switch comparison concerns the heavy-chain constant-region arrangement.

questions.title: Population timing versus an individual record
questions.subject: genetics
questions.prompt: A known fictional lineage is observed only at (V0, Cmu) and later (V1, Cgamma). A separate study reports a predominant event order in its analyzed population. What can these statements establish about this lineage?

options.text: Both displayed features differ, but this lineage’s missing intermediate is not identified.
options.explanation: The endpoint labels show the two feature differences. A population pattern does not supply an observation of this particular missing intermediate.

options.text: The variable change certainly occurred first, because it is written first in the pair.
options.explanation: Coordinate order in a symbol is not an event timeline. The worksheet displays no intermediate observation.

options.text: The class switch certainly occurred first, because a predominant population pattern proves every individual history.
options.explanation: A typical or predominant result does not establish every individual trajectory. The specific lineage still needs its own evidence.

questions.title: A shared factor and separate outcomes
questions.subject: genetics
questions.prompt: A controlled experimental comparison reports that removing AID disrupts both a class-switch readout and a variable-region mutation readout in the tested system. Which inference stays within that result?

options.text: The perturbation affects both tested outcomes, without proving that they are one process.
options.explanation: A shared experimental requirement can link distinct outcomes. The result does not identify every molecular step or collapse the readouts into one operation.

options.text: The two outcomes are identical, because they share an affected factor.
options.explanation: Different processes can depend on a common factor. Separate readouts do not become identical merely because one perturbation affects both.

options.text: AID is the only molecule involved, because removing it changes both readouts.
options.explanation: The experiment does not test or exclude every other participating molecule. A requirement is not a complete inventory of the mechanism.

questions.title: Nerve bundles and muscle targets
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: In a fictional topology, trunk T divides into bundles A and B. They reach two regions of the same muscle M, and individual axons are not traced. What follows?

options.text: Two named terminal bundles and one unique muscle target; the axon count is unspecified.
options.explanation: The counted bundle labels are A and B, while both destinations belong to M. The schematic does not trace individual axons.

options.text: Two muscle targets and exactly two motor axons.
options.explanation: Two regions of one muscle are not two muscles, and bundle labels do not establish how many axons they contain.

options.text: Two independently activated muscle compartments have been demonstrated physiologically.
options.explanation: The supplied connection diagram has no neural-activity, contraction or force measurements. Functional independence is an additional claim.

questions.title: Open an equal branch at fixed driving pressure
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: In a fictional steady model, a path has resistance 4 pressure-units per flow-unit and driving pressure difference 8 pressure-units. A second resistance 4 connects directly in parallel between the same fixed pressure nodes. What is supported?

options.text: Equivalent resistance is 2; total flow becomes 4 while each branch carries 2.
options.explanation: Each branch sees the stipulated 8 pressure-units, so each flow is 8/4 = 2 flow-units and the flows add. The original branch has not lost driving pressure.

options.text: Each branch must carry 1 because a fixed total flow is split.
options.explanation: The model fixes pressure, not total flow. Assuming fixed total flow changes the controller.

options.text: Equivalent resistance becomes 8 because two resistances are present.
options.explanation: Adding resistances directly is the series rule. These two paths are parallel.

questions.title: Find the actual branch pressure
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: In a fictional steady model, a shared upstream resistance 2 is in series before two parallel resistances 4. Total driving pressure difference is 12 pressure-units. Resistances use pressure-units per flow-unit and stay fixed. Which branch result follows?

options.text: Each branch sees pressure difference 6 and carries 1.5 flow-units.
options.explanation: The pair has equivalent resistance 2, total resistance is 4 and total flow is 3. The shared segment drops 6 pressure-units, leaving 6 across each branch.

options.text: Each branch sees all 12 and carries 3 flow-units.
options.explanation: That ignores the pressure drop across the shared upstream resistance and would not satisfy the stated complete network.

options.text: Each branch sees pressure difference 3 because there are four resistance-units in total.
options.explanation: A resistance value is not a count of equal pressure divisions. Calculate the shared flow and each segment’s drop.

questions.title: Keep the flow controller explicit
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: In a fictional steady model, an ideal controller holds total flow at 4 flow-units. A single resistance 4 is replaced by two resistances 4 directly in parallel. Resistances use pressure-units per flow-unit. Which new driving pressure and branch flows are consistent?

options.text: Driving pressure difference is 8 pressure-units; each branch carries 2 flow-units.
options.explanation: The equivalent resistance is 2, so ΔP = Q_total × R_equivalent = 4 × 2 = 8 pressure-units. Equal branches then carry 2 flow-units each.

options.text: Driving pressure difference is 16 pressure-units; each branch carries 4 flow-units while total flow stays 4.
options.explanation: Those branch flows would sum to 8, contradicting the stipulated total flow of 4 flow-units.

options.text: Driving pressure stays fixed solely because the branches are parallel.
options.explanation: Parallel branches share their own node pressure difference, but that value can change when total flow rather than pressure is controlled.

questions.title: Count the defined neuron, not the branches
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: In fictional Model A, P and C are peripheral and central processes of the same neuron S. They meet at J, with a short stem from J to S’s soma. No synapse is specified at J. What follows for this model?

options.text: Two neurons and one obligatory neuronal synapse at J
options.explanation: That counts the two named branches as separate neurons. The model explicitly assigns both to S and specifies no synapse at J.

options.text: One neuron, two named functional branches and no specified neuronal synapse at J
options.explanation: The model defines one continuous cell with two named branches. Branching does not by itself add another neuron or an intercellular synapse.

options.text: Three neurons, one for each of the three drawn segments
options.explanation: The model explicitly makes all three segments parts of S. Segments within a branching cell are not separate neurons.

questions.title: Locate the two cell bodies
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: Fictional Model B contains neuron N1 with its soma in the CNS. N1 makes one specified synapse on N2, whose soma is in a peripheral autonomic ganglion. N2 sends an axon to an effector. Counting only this defined path, which statement follows?

options.text: Both neuronal somata must be inside the peripheral ganglion
options.explanation: The model places N1’s soma in the CNS. Its axon reaching the ganglion does not move that soma there.

options.text: The ganglion contains no neuronal soma because the path has an effector
options.explanation: N2’s soma is explicitly in the ganglion; its axon can continue to an effector.

options.text: The path has two neurons, with one of their somata inside the peripheral ganglion
options.explanation: N1 and N2 are separate neurons, but only N2’s soma is placed in the ganglion. This is not a total count of all cells in an actual ganglion.

questions.title: Separate visible profiles from an inferred circuit
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: A fictional tissue description reports large neuronal cell-body profiles, several nearby small dark nuclei and pale spaces around some somata. It does not show complete processes or specialised synaptic detail. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: It supports a neuronal cell-body region with neighbouring cells, while exact small-cell identities and the complete circuit remain unresolved
options.explanation: The description supplies somatic profiles and neighbouring nuclei. It does not identify every nucleus, reconstruct a branch point or demonstrate a functional synapse.

options.text: Every small dark nucleus must belong to one satellite glial cell for each neuron
options.explanation: Position can support an interpretation, but this description does not exclude other cell types or establish a fixed ratio.

options.text: Every pale space around a soma proves compact myelin
options.explanation: Preparation can leave spaces around cell profiles. A halo alone does not demonstrate a compact multilamellar myelin sheath.

questions.title: Match a research claim to its evidence
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: The cited Kumari study concerns neuron-satellite-glia relationships in mouse sympathetic ganglia. A student then sees small nuclei near human neuronal somata in an ordinary section. What is the appropriate interpretation?

options.text: The nuclei alone reproduce the study’s activity measurements
options.explanation: A structural appearance in another preparation is not an activity recording.

options.text: Keep the study’s organism, tissue and measured outcomes distinct from the human section’s limited structural evidence
options.explanation: Evidence must match the claim. The research context and the routine section cannot silently be treated as equivalent measurements.

options.text: The study proves that every peripheral ganglion has the same glial cell ratio
options.explanation: The cited study does not establish that universal ratio, and the described section does not supply a complete count.

questions.subject: biochemistry
questions.title: Separate gross events from net change
questions.prompt: A fictional isolated ledger specifies 100 forward and 70 reverse SHMT reaction events, sufficient reactants and no side reactions. Which accounting statement follows?

options.text: 170 net forward events
options.explanation: Adding both directions gives gross events. Reverse events oppose the forward net change.

options.text: 170 total defined events and 30 net forward events
options.explanation: Total events add 100 + 70; their opposing net changes subtract 100 − 70. Neither number is a measured cellular rate or concentration.

options.text: 70 net reverse events
options.explanation: That omits the 100 specified forward events. The defined difference is 30 forward.

questions.subject: biochemistry
questions.title: Read the reaction before its cofactor label
questions.prompt: A student recognises PLP in the stated SHMT context and concludes that the written reaction must transfer an amino group and directly produce urea. Which correction is justified?

options.text: Every PLP-associated reaction has identical net products
options.explanation: A shared catalytic cofactor does not make two different reaction equations identical.

options.text: Amino-acid participation alone proves nitrogen has left the body
options.explanation: Participation in a reaction is not excretion. The equation does not state that nitrogen has left the system.

options.text: Read the named reaction and its products; the cofactor name alone does not establish that claim
options.explanation: The stated serine/folate relationship names glycine and the folate-bound carbon unit. Urea is not a product in that net equation.

questions.subject: biochemistry
questions.title: Keep the study context attached
questions.prompt: The cited structural abstract describes a particular ligand-bound murine SHMT complex. Which conclusion stays within the evidence?

options.text: Identify the organism, ligand and experimental state before relating it to the separately written reaction
options.explanation: The structural complex and the reaction equation answer different questions; their folate names and contexts must remain distinct.

options.text: The structure alone measures net reaction flux in a human tissue
options.explanation: A ligand-bound mouse-enzyme structure is not a human tissue-flux measurement.

options.text: The bound formyl-folate name can replace the methylene-folate product name everywhere
options.explanation: The different chemical forms are not interchangeable labels.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: What can a single unlabeled lung section reliably establish about gestational age?

options.text: It can support a tentative structural interpretation, but does not by itself establish a precise age.
options.explanation: Development overlaps in time and space, and preparation and sampling affect what is visible.

options.text: It identifies the exact week without other information.
options.explanation: A section lacks enough contextual and developmental information for exact dating.

options.text: It directly measures lung function.
options.explanation: Structure in an isolated section is not a direct functional measurement.

questions.title: Interpret a section without inventing its age

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: A fictional tracing task states that sixteen profiles come from eight traced airways. Which statement retains the supplied observation units?

options.text: There must be sixteen different airways.
